extracted.intended_audience: medical communicators, medical editors, and authors reporting randomized controlled trials
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing manuscript reports of randomized controlled trials using the CONSORT 2010 checklist and flow diagram to ensure complete, clear, and transparent reporting (especially for parallel, 2-group trials).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the CONSORT 25-item checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the 25-item checklist of essential items authors need to include to ensure complete and transparent reporting of a randomized trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The checklist covers items across the IMRAD structure (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) and is the core tool for ensuring reporting completeness; it is reproduced in articles discussing the statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flow diagram for subject progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a flow diagram showing how subjects progress through the phases of a parallel randomized trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The flow diagram illustrates the process of a parallel randomized trial and, together with the checklist, creates a clear and cohesive picture of the randomization process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title identifies the study as randomized
rubrics_metrics.description: The title of the trial should identify it as a randomized trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly stating 'randomized' in the title helps readers immediately recognize the study design and facilitates indexing and retrieval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract reflects trial design and findings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Abstract should reflect the trial’s design, methods, results, and conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complete abstract summarizes key elements of design and findings so readers can assess relevance and validity quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction: background and objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the scientific background and rationale and state specific objectives or hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The checklist asks authors to include background and objectives to frame the trial’s importance and intended contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: trial design
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the trial design (eg, parallel group, cluster), including allocation ratio and any important changes to methods after trial commencement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The checklist’s Methods section focuses on clear description of the overall design so readers can understand how the trial was structured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: participants (eligibility and settings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report eligibility criteria for participants and the settings and locations where the data were collected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear reporting of participant selection and setting enables assessment of generalizability and potential selection bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: interventions (detailed description)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe interventions for each group with sufficient details to allow replication, including how and when they were actually administered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed intervention descriptions support reproducibility and interpretation of observed effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: outcomes (pre-specified and measured)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define pre-specified primary and secondary outcome measures and how and when they were assessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear outcome definitions prevent post-hoc switching and aid interpretation of effect sizes and clinical relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: sample size
rubrics_metrics.description: Report how sample size was determined, including any calculations, assumptions, and any interim analyses or stopping rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparent sample-size justification helps readers judge study power and risk of type I/II errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: sequence generation (randomization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the method used to generate the random allocation sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting sequence generation methods (e.g., computer random number generator, minimization) is key to assessing allocation randomness and selection bias risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: allocation concealment mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the mechanism used to implement the random allocation sequence and any steps taken to conceal allocation until interventions were assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocation concealment details (e.g., sealed envelopes, central randomization) are critical to prevent selection bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: implementation of randomization
rubrics_metrics.description: Report who generated the sequence, who enrolled participants, and who assigned participants to interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifying roles in the randomization process helps readers evaluate the risk of manipulation or errors in assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: blinding (masking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe whether participants, those administering interventions, and those assessing outcomes were blinded to group assignment, and how blinding was achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blinding details inform assessment of performance and detection bias and the credibility of outcome assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: statistical methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe statistical methods used to compare groups for primary and secondary outcomes, including methods for additional analyses and handling of missing data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed statistical reporting allows appraisal of appropriateness of analyses and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results: participant flow
rubrics_metrics.description: Report numbers of participants at each stage (enrollment, allocation, follow-up, analysis) and account for losses and exclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participant flow information, often shown in the CONSORT flow diagram, is essential to assess attrition bias and the integrity of the randomized groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results: recruitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Report dates defining the periods of recruitment and follow-up and why the trial ended or was stopped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recruitment timing and reasons for early stopping inform potential biases related to temporal effects or premature termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results: baseline data
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a table of baseline demographic and clinical characteristics for each group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baseline data allow readers to assess comparability of groups after randomization and potential confounding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results: numbers analyzed
rubrics_metrics.description: Report number of participants included in each analysis and whether analyses were by original assigned groups (intention-to-treat).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifying denominators and analytic populations clarifies interpretability of estimated effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results: outcomes and estimation
rubrics_metrics.description: Present results for each primary and secondary outcome, estimated effect size and its precision (e.g., 95% CI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting effect sizes with confidence intervals supports clinical and statistical interpretation beyond p-values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results: ancillary analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Report results of any other analyses performed, including subgroup and adjusted analyses, and specify which were pre-specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishing pre-specified from exploratory analyses guards against overinterpretation of chance findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results: harms
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe all important harms or unintended effects in each group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting adverse events is necessary for balanced appraisal of benefits versus risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion: limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss trial limitations, potential biases, imprecision, and the direction and magnitude of possible bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit limitations help readers judge the strength of evidence and generalizability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other information: funding and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Report sources of funding, role of funders, and where the full protocol and data (if applicable) can be accessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency about funding and protocol accessibility helps detect conflicts of interest and enables verification or secondary analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: applicability to parallel, 2-group trials and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: The CONSORT 2010 Statement is especially useful for reporting randomized, controlled, 2-group, parallel trials; other extensions and resources exist for different trial designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the main CONSORT checklist and flow diagram for parallel trials; consult CONSORT extensions (e.g., for cluster trials, non-inferiority trials) when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting-only scope (not design or conduct guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: CONSORT addresses reporting of what was done and what was found; it does not give recommendations for designing, conducting, or analyzing trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should use CONSORT to improve completeness and transparency of reporting but rely on methodological guidance elsewhere for trial design/analysis decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underlying principle: complete, clear, and transparent reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure reports provide complete and transparent information on methodology and findings so readers can accurately assess validity and reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biased results from poorly designed and reported trials can mislead decision making; adherence to CONSORT promotes clarity that supports evidence-based decisions at clinical and policy levels.
